what: The §3.6 assumption ledger: every unproved thing a spine chain stands on, one row each, with a statement, a probe command, a discharge condition, a date and an owning job. designs/2026-08-22-spine-and-lattice-program.md §3.6 and standing rule R8.
not_claimed: This file is an INVENTORY OF STATED ASSUMPTIONS, not evidence that any of them is safe. A row's presence is a debt, not a discharge. A row carrying a witness is a BOUNDED assumption, not a closed one. And the ledger cannot be complete by construction: the derived classes are as complete as their source artifacts, and the seeded classes are as complete as the humans who wrote them down. docs/analysis/spine-assumption-ledger-2026-08-27.md states this at length.
counting_rule: `count` counts rows with status=measured — the debt standing today, and the number G-SCORE ratchets DOWN. `prospective_count` counts rows for assumptions of jobs that have NOT RUN; they are listed so §3.6's named contracts are visible, and excluded from `count` so a planned assumption never masquerades as a live one. A prospective row becoming live is a rebase of `count` upward, and it is progress.

cross_references.why_not_copied: Ring R2 lane (b) mints and ratchets its own §3.6 rows in its own artifact. Copying them here would give each assumption two accounting points and two ratchets; the env-bypass census follows the same rule. They are counted in the scoreboard by the separate row `assumption_ledger.verdict_io_lane_b`, which is disjoint from `assumption_ledger.count` by construction — this generator aborts if any id here collides with one there.

entries.statement: The crystal-A2 mint erases this slot from the projected core module, and every chain minted through that projection stands, unproved, on the erasure being invisible to the value the module computes. SLOT: Calling convention and linkage of the FUNCTION (closed) and of each direct call site (open, and open for a different reason than the row used to give). ARTIFACT CARRIES: `rustcc fn @level::Level::is_zero(functy.0) {` -- the `rustcc` IS the calling convention. `trust_ir::display`'s `impl Display for Function` prints the linkage when it is not `External` and the convention when it is not `C`, in that order, before `fn @`. All sixteen committed fixtures are `external` + `rustcc`, the first suppressed and the second printed. CORE CARRIES: Nothing for the function. UNCHANGED. `callindirect` DOES carry a convention operand in the fragment; a direct `call` does not, because `trust_ir::Inst::Call` has no such field. STATE IN THE OWNING ARTIFACT (compared): CLOSED 2026-08-20 for the FUNCTION, as a comparison. A body whose header names a different convention or a different linkage is refused BY NAME (`calling convention: the artifact carries [ccc]; the chain's tag table pins [rustcc]`), and a header with no keyword at all is read as `external`/`ccc` -- a value -- rather than as whatever the pin says. An unrecognised leading token is refused rather than skipped, so a linkage or convention trust-ir grows later cannot be read as `no token`. RESIDUAL: STILL OPEN, and now stated at its real shape: the calling convention of a DIRECT CALL's callee. `trust_ir::Inst::Call` is `{ callee, args }` and carries no convention field at all, so this is not an erasure by the printer -- it is absent from the IR. The convention of a direct callee is a property of the callee's own `Function`, which is not in a one-function fragment, so the slot becomes witnessable when the fragment grows past one function and not before. The one convention the fragment DOES carry, on `callindirect`, is proved inert: `ir_exec_callind_conv_irrelevant` proves `ir_exec` returns the same IRConfig at any two conventions. So the residual is a CROSS-FUNCTION residual, not a text-reader blindness.

SLOT: WHICH block a function is entered at. ARTIFACT CARRIES: `trust_ir::Function` has an `entry: BlockId` field SEPARATE from its `blocks: Vec<Block>`. The emitted TEXT prints the blocks in vector order and prints NO entry marker at all. CORE CARRIES: `(entry N)` -- the id of the FIRST block reader B encountered, and reader A's reading of the real `func.entry`. STATE IN THE OWNING ARTIFACT (unwitnessed): OPEN, and open at the PRODUCER rather than at this gate -- which is why it is a row and not a defect. Two functions differing only in their entry block have BYTE-IDENTICAL emitted text, so no text reader can separate them and no amount of work on reader B can change that. What keeps it from being a hole is that reader A does NOT assume: it reads `func.entry` off the binary. So a body whose entry is not its first block makes readers A and B DISAGREE, and M2 is the check that fires. The assumption is therefore CHECKED rather than merely made -- but it was checked by accident, and until 2026-08-20 nothing said so. RESIDUAL: There is no in-repo witness. Constructing one needs a `trust_ir::Module` built by hand with `entry != blocks[0]`, serialised and re-read, which is a producer-side test in the `trust` repo. Until then this is a single-assumption slot whose only defence is that two readers derive it differently and are compared.

entries.statement: The designated target's link-4 theorems hold over a module whose second function is AUTHORED, not minted. `ir_lzb_correct` (A4) and `ir_lzb_machine_sound` (A5) are stated over `ir_lzb_module` = the minted `ir_lz_func` at function 0 (pinned by name, kernel-checked, `ir_lzb_func0_is_minted`) PLUS a hand-authored model of `<LevelArc as Deref>::deref` at function 1. That model is an ASSUMPTION about `Option::as_deref` + `Option::expect`, whose bodies no artifact here can carry: rustc has no cross-crate THIR (`thir_body` takes a `LocalDefId`; there is no `thir_of_instance`). Measured 2026-08-26, the scope was an undercount in both directions: the reachable closure is six or seven functions, not two, it includes the higher-order `Option::map`, and its DATA path bottoms out at `NonNull::as_ref`'s `&*ptr` — a language primitive with no body at all, which unreachability cannot excuse because dereferencing is what `is_zero` is there to do. Every chain that reads through an `Arc` inherits this floor.
entries.discharge: replace the authored model with a DERIVED one via cross-crate lowering (designs/2026-08-26-cross-crate-lowering-for-a0.md). Note what that buys, in the currency the status page states: it does not REMOVE the assumption, it converts a bespoke one ("`deref` does load + null-check + assert", this chain only) into shared instruction semantics ("EvalIR's `load` models `&*ptr`") that all eighteen chains already rest on. This row closes only when the deref's own callees are bodyful — A0's bodyful reachable closure, architecturally blocked today.

entries.statement: The niche-encoding obligation, the older of the designated target's two layout obligations. Measured from the BINARY dumps (data/crystal_enum_layout_census_2026-08-21.json, two sealed producers, control/subject/iso arms, all six agreeing), `Level` is NICHE-encoded — `Niche{untagged=4 (Param), niche_variants=0..=3, niche_start=3, niche_offset=0, niche_ty=u64}`, size 40, align 8, `repr=None`. The model side's `u8` tag exists only through `canonical_tag_repr()`'s `smallest_for` fallback, and the emitted `Level` bodies read `extractfield u8 %v, 0` and switch on discriminant VALUES 0..4 — so the text form and the layout descriptor disagree about where that number lives. The disagreement is printed, not smoothed; the chain still stands on the model's tag encoding for `Level`, unproved. Stage 2 made the assumption source-guaranteed for the three FIELDLESS enums (a `repr(u8)` fieldless enum IS a `u8`); `Level` is not one of them, and its repr flip stays a separate differentially-gated change.
entries.discharge: land the `Level` repr flip as a differentially-gated subject change (R4: it ships as the kernel, passes corpus verdict-parity and re-earns every affected chain), or prove the niche encoding and the model's tag agree at every constructor.
